about.title: Placerville Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Placerville is small enough—about 10,650 residents—that a sudden death is rarely anonymous here. In 2025, public records logged 31 injury collisions inside the city limits, 51 people hurt, and one traffic death. One is a low number until it is your family. Reported crashes in Placerville cluster along Route 50, Placerville Drive, and Broadway Drive, most often on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. If someone you love was killed because another person was careless—behind the wheel, on a job site, in a care setting—California law allows certain family members to bring a civil wrongful death claim. That claim runs on its own track, apart from any criminal case the El Dorado County District Attorney may pursue, and it has a two-year deadline that shrinks when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We listen first, then connect you with an independent attorney who handles these matters on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases: a spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can sort out who in your family qualifies before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, but the window is much shorter when a city, county, or state agency is involved. An early connection means those dates are calendared while your family focuses on grieving.

items.title: The full picture of your loss
items.desc: Recoverable losses go beyond funeral and burial costs to include the financial support your loved one would have provided and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Your attorney works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My spouse was killed in a crash on US-50 near Placerville. Does the criminal case decide our claim?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action, entirely separate from any charges the district attorney may bring, and it can move forward whether or not a criminal case is filed or results in a conviction. The CHP or Placerville Police collision report will matter as evidence, but the two proceedings have different standards and different goals. An attorney can request that report and preserve other evidence from the scene while it is still available.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California gives first priority to the surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children of the person who died. If there are none, certain other heirs and financially dependent family members may have standing. Because the rules can get complicated in blended families, it helps to have an attorney confirm who should be named before a claim is filed.

items.question: How long do we have to act, and what if a government vehicle or road agency was involved?
items.answer: For most wrongful death claims in California, the deadline is two years from the date of death. If a public entity—such as Caltrans, El Dorado County, or the City of Placerville—may share responsibility, a formal government claim generally has to be presented within six months, well before any lawsuit. Given how quickly that window closes, it is wise to speak with an attorney sooner rather than later.
